coverage_note: all 50 reserved IDs received a literal full-statement screen; dispositions below; metadata tags were not treated as technical review

dispositions.reason: Asks for a representative subclass of Calderon-Zygmund operators implying L^p(w) bounds for all CZOs via Tolsa's theorem; resolving requires new sparse-domination structure theory. No tractable full-scope mechanism at screening.
Exact extremal numbers ex(n,B_{5,2}), ex(n,B_{6,2}) for all large n is a famous open hypergraph Turan problem; exact determination for fixed books is far beyond screening-level methods.

Literal statement fully answered negatively by exact counterexample f=(z+5)^3 -> sum b_i A_i = x^2+19x+216 (disc -503; zero real roots by exact Sturm). BUT prior art: Branden-Jochemko disproved Brenti's conjecture that the shifted Eulerian transformation A^o (x^n -> x A_n(x)) preserves real-rootedness on real-nonpositive-root polynomials (same hypothesis class), and Athanasiadis (arXiv:2302.00754, JLMS 2025) proved the positive family P_n[x]; the residual delta is a one-line shift. Ranked #3 with recommendation: allocate only if root judges the unshifted-statement counterexample + maximal-positive-cone classification non-derivative.

"A good way to compute Z(G) for planar/outerplanar G" is not a crisp mathematical target; the natural crisp version (complexity of zero forcing on planar graphs) is a hardness question with no low-hanging mechanism noted.
Quantum query-complexity question (beating Grover for range-search/threshold). Open-ended; any full-scope answer needs new quantum algorithm or oracle lower bound machinery.

"How short can units in Q[x]/(x^312-x^156-1) be" reduces to shortest-vector-type questions in a rank-156 unit lattice; true minimum is SVP-hard territory and any honest computation exceeds fixed caps. Observation retained: alpha (root of x^312-x^156-1) is a unit with house phi^(1/156) ~ 1.00309, and alpha-1 is also a unit (Norm=1).
Centralizers in Artin groups / Euclidean Artin group commutation criterion is an active hard area; no screening-level mechanism.
Donaldson question: smooth solutions of a degenerate PDE on M x [0,1] (Hamilton/Perelman-type equation with lambda>0); deep geometric analysis.
Weil-etale topos cohomology for arithmetic schemes; deep arithmetic geometry, far from low-hanging.

Literally, pairing-friendly curves of embedding degree k=13 exist by the Cocks-Pinch construction (works for every k, ~2002), so the literal question predates-resolved; the intended question (low rho / efficient families for k=13) requires a large computational search. Neither variant is a low-hanging novel full-scope target.
Nonvanishing proportion of L(1/2, chi_d) weighted twisted sums: deep analytic number theory (moment methods, family laws).
Set-theoretic forcing: model of TP_kappa for all regular kappa in [aleph_2, aleph_{omega^2+2}]; deep consistency machinery.
"Exhibit a model with 3 phase transitions" for basis-pursuit-type problems is open-ended and not crisply quantified; no decidable exact target.
Short algebraic definition of a tetracategory: a large coherence-data problem; even tricategory definitions run tens of pages.

Kourovka 21.9 (free pro-p F: finite family of open subgroups so that only trivial subgroup is characteristic in each). Screening found no concrete tractable mechanism; characteristic-subgroup structure of free pro-p groups is delicate. Bounded screen only, not exhaustive.
